title: Cloud Practitioner Exam Readiness
description: Gauge how ready you are for an entry-level cloud practitioner certification exam. Five exam-style questions sample the whole program — service models, deployment models, security, and cost — and your score maps to a readiness level with guidance on what to revise next.

questions.prompt: A company wants to stop managing email servers entirely and have staff simply sign in to a hosted email application through the browser. Which service model are they adopting?

options.label: Infrastructure as a Service (IaaS)
Platform as a Service (PaaS)
Software as a Service (SaaS)
Function as a Service (FaaS)

questions.explanation: A fully hosted application consumed through a browser with nothing to install or manage is SaaS — the provider runs everything from the hardware up to the application itself.

questions.prompt: Under the shared responsibility model, which of the following is always the CUSTOMER'S responsibility, regardless of service model?

options.label: Physical security of the data centres
Managing user access permissions and account credentials
Replacing failed hard drives in the provider's servers
Maintaining the provider's core network backbone

questions.explanation: The provider secures the cloud itself — facilities, hardware, and core network — but who may access your data and how identities are protected is always on the customer's side of the line.

questions.prompt: A regulated bank must keep customer records on infrastructure it controls, but wants public cloud elasticity for its marketing website. Which deployment approach satisfies both requirements?

options.label: Move everything to a single public cloud region
A hybrid cloud: sensitive systems on private infrastructure, the website in the public cloud
Keep everything on-premises and buy more servers for traffic spikes
A community cloud shared with other banks' customer data

questions.explanation: Hybrid cloud is the standard answer when regulation pins some data to controlled infrastructure while other workloads benefit from public cloud scale — each system runs where its constraints demand.

questions.prompt: Which combination of actions best protects a new cloud account on day one?

options.label: Enable MFA on the root user, create a separate admin user, and set a billing alert
Write the root password in a shared team chat and start building
Grant all team members full administrator access to save time
Disable all security features until the first application is live

questions.explanation: MFA on root, an everyday admin user in place of root, and a billing alarm are the three cheapest, highest-value protections — they guard against account takeover and surprise bills before any workload exists.

questions.prompt: An application's users across West Africa complain that downloading its static images is slow because the servers are hosted in Europe. Which service most directly addresses this?

options.label: A larger virtual machine in the same European region
A content delivery network caching the images at edge locations near the users
A second database replica in Europe
Switching from object storage to block storage

questions.explanation: A CDN caches static content at edge locations close to users, cutting the distance data travels — the direct remedy when latency to a far-away region makes static content slow.

title: Cloud For Beginners Final Assessment
description: The capstone for the Cloud For Beginners module. It combines multiple-choice questions covering the module's key concepts with a practical submission where you apply what you learned to a small architecture exercise.

questions.prompt: Which statement correctly orders the service models from most customer-managed to least customer-managed?

options.label: SaaS → PaaS → IaaS
IaaS → PaaS → SaaS
PaaS → IaaS → SaaS
IaaS → SaaS → PaaS

questions.explanation: With IaaS you manage everything above the infrastructure; PaaS hands the platform to the provider; with SaaS the provider manages the entire stack, leaving you only the application to use.

questions.prompt: A startup with unpredictable growth and no capital for hardware needs to launch quickly. Which deployment model do its constraints point to?

options.label: Private cloud in its own data centre
Community cloud with other startups
Public cloud
No cloud — buy used servers

questions.explanation: Zero upfront cost, pay-as-you-go pricing, and instant elasticity make the public cloud the natural fit for a startup that cannot predict its growth or fund hardware purchases.

questions.prompt: Before migrating a workload, which prerequisite most directly prevents a surprise bill in the first month?

options.label: Choosing a memorable name for the project
Setting up billing alerts and estimating monthly cost at realistic usage
Buying reserved capacity for three years immediately
Migrating all workloads at once to finish faster

questions.explanation: A cost estimate sets expectations and a billing alert catches drift early — together they turn a forgotten test server into an email notification instead of an invoice shock.
